name: DegenLens On-Chain Intelligence
description:
DegenLens reads live blockchain state straight from node RPC and returns the evidence behind each answer, not just a verdict. It adds what a generic RPC reader cannot: a curated registry of gambling-operator wallet clusters, used to identify who an address is actually settling with.

ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP — from a transaction hash: succeeded or reverted, sender and recipient, whether it was a transfer, a contract call and which function, or a deployment, the value moved, block, gas and fee, and the ERC-20 transfers in its receipt. An unknown hash is reported as not found, never guessed.

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK — from an address or ENS name: native-coin and token balances at a stated block, plus the reviewed operator clusters that address has recently touched. An unresolvable ENS name is reported as such, never answered against another account. An unreadable balance is unknown, never zero — an empty wallet and a dead provider are different facts.

FRAUD_DETECTION — from an address or transaction: five screens (round-trip returns, transfer velocity, counterparty concentration, dust fan-in, repeated identical amounts), returning a bounded risk tier with every measurement, so a low-risk answer carries the evidence a high-risk one would. Exchanges, bridges, routers and gambling operators are identified as counterparties, so ordinary settlement is not flagged as suspicious. Tiers rank review priority and are never a finding of fraud: the chain records settlement, not intent.

Attribution covers 65 reviewed wallets across Stake.com, Rollbit, BC.Game, Shuffle.com and Yeet on eight chains, each labelled hot, cold or consolidation and carrying its evidence status, so a caller can weigh the claim rather than trust it. It is an ownership claim about an address, not about any person, and an operator transfer is settlement, not proof of a wager.

Every answer states its confidence, source and coverage; a partial read is said plainly. Chains: ethereum, base, polygon, arbitrum, optimism, bsc, avalanche, solana, tron, bitcoin, where the operation is available.

endpoints.description: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Look up one specific EVM transaction by its complete 0x-prefixed 64-hex-character hash. Returns confirmed, reverted, pending, or not_found plus sender, recipient, native value, block, gas used, effective gas price, total fee, method identifier, and decoded ERC-20 transfers. Use only when the question supplies an actual transaction hash. This is not a wallet-balance or fraud endpoint.

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Return the current native-coin and token balances of one specific blockchain address or ENS name on a named chain. The address is required. Returns exact native base units, human-readable native amount, asset symbol, block height, and token balances. An unreadable provider returns unavailable, never a fabricated zero. This endpoint answers what an account currently holds; it does not assess fraud.

FRAUD_DETECTION. Assess how likely the specific entity, transaction, or action named in the required natural-language query is to be fraudulent. For an on-chain address, screen round-trip returns, transfer velocity, counterparty concentration, dust fan-in, and repeated identical amounts. For a transaction hash, screen its sender and return transaction context. Reviewed named cases receive a concise source-backed factual answer; unknown off-chain subjects are reported out_of_coverage rather than guessed. Returns a bounded risk_score, risk_tier, concise verdict, and measurements for on-chain subjects.

name: LiveCert Operational Signals
description: Deterministic operational signals. /ssl-check performs a live TLS handshake against a domain and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now: valid, expired, self-signed, untrusted, or issued for a different hostname, with issuer, validity window and days remaining. Unlike certificate-transparency lookups, which report what was issued, this reports what is deployed — the two disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. /storm-alert reports severe-weather disruption risk for a named location over the next 48 hours, graded on Beaufort gust thresholds and thunderstorm forecasts, for logistics and risk agents that need to know about storms rather than current conditions. /weather-forecast reports future conditions for a location over a stated window: the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, total precipitation and peak wind. All three answers are deterministic and independently checkable.

Structured extraction from text supplied inline in the question. Reads quantities and units, contact details, named entities, action items, dates and events, or bare numeric values, and answers with the extracted fields themselves. The text is carried in the question, so nothing is fetched and the answer is deterministic and checkable against the input.

Current news headlines for a topic and optional region, read live from Google News at request time and returned as a numbered list with each source named. Honours a requested count such as "top 5". Headlines rotate, so the answer states the date it was read.

Native-coin balance of an EVM address, read with eth_getBalance at the latest block from public JSON-RPC on the chain the question names — Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism or Polygon. A zero balance is reported as zero; an RPC that does not answer is reported as unavailable rather than as zero. Token balances such as USDT are not included, and the answer says so when one was asked about.

A specific claim, looked up against a citable encyclopaedic reference and reported with the article named and quoted. Reports an explicit refutation when the source states one, and otherwise says plainly that the source does not settle the claim. It does not adjudicate contested claims and never asserts that a claim is true on the strength of a topical match.

Questions about Telegraph itself — miner registration and the YAML registry, the canonical intent set, how answers are scored, the Explorer and leaderboard, and the hackathon. Live figures such as the number of registered miners or the miners serving a named intent are read from the protocol at request time rather than recalled. Questions outside those areas are answered as not covered, with a pointer to the protocol documentation, rather than guessed.

Statistical authorship analysis of a supplied passage. Measures sentence-length burstiness, type-token ratio, repeated word pairs and formulaic connectives, and reports what they indicate with a calibrated confidence that is capped at 0.6. Authorship detection is not reliable enough to treat as proof and the answer says so; when no passage long enough to analyse is supplied it says that instead of guessing.

verdict.description: The answer's label, and its vocabulary is per endpoint. /ssl-check returns a certificate state (valid, expired, not_yet_valid, hostname_mismatch, self_signed, untrusted, unreachable); /storm-alert a storm-risk grade (none, low, moderate, high, severe); /weather-forecast a condition (clear, mostly clear, cloudy, fog, drizzle, rain, heavy rain, snow, thunderstorms); /translate "translated"; /papers "papers"; /ai-detect likely_human, likely_ai or inconclusive; and /ip-geolocate the resolved place itself, or the class of a special-use range (private, reserved, loopback, link_local, shared, multicast, broadcast). Any endpoint returns "unknown" when it could not answer. A closed enum was declared here previously and four endpoints did not conform to it, /ip-geolocate least of all because a place name cannot be enumerated.

name: TxLens
description:
TxLens answers on-chain and market questions with a single verifiable number or status sourced from live providers. Short-lived caches reduce repeated provider calls, and freshness timestamps identify when the data was fetched.
It covers fourteen canonical intents. WEATHER_FORECAST: what will the weather do at a named place on the day or over the window asked about, answering the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, freeze, temperature) rather than reciting a range. STORM_ALERT: how disruptive will the weather be at a place over the next 48 hours, graded and scored with the operational response it calls for. ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP: given a transaction hash, is it confirmed, reverted, pending or not found, and what did it do. GAS_PRICE: what does a transaction cost right now on a named chain. WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK: what native coin or ERC-20 token does a given address hold. TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT: how many distinct addresses hold a token. TVL_LOOKUP: how much value is locked in a named DeFi protocol or chain. CRYPTO_PRICE: what is a coin or on-chain token worth in USD. STOCK_PRICE: what is a listed equity trading at. SSL_VERIFICATION: is a domain's TLS certificate valid and when does it expire, from a real live handshake. IP_GEOLOCATION: where is an IPv4 or IPv6 address, on whose network, and is it a proxy, VPN or datacenter address. ACADEMIC_SEARCH: which peer-reviewed papers exist on a topic, with journal, authors, citation counts and DOIs. WEB_SEARCH: an open question of any kind, answered from a live web search with the sources named, for the questions that have no single authoritative feed behind them. FRAUD_DETECTION: how likely is a given address or scheme to be fraudulent.
Blockscout-backed reads cover five EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon). RPC-backed reads currently cover Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum and Polygon because the current Ankr key does not include Optimism. Each signal comes from a live provider or a bounded short-lived cache, and every answer carries a complete plain-language `summary` that states the verdict and then each thing actually checked, a deterministic `canonical` string for hashing, and a 0-1 `confidence` that reflects real certainty rather than a fixed constant: forecast confidence falls with range, and IP geolocation is reported at 0.95 because it is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city.
Every endpoint accepts the caller's whole question in place of its structured parameter, and answers it, rather than refusing input that is not already reduced to a bare parameter.

endpoints.description: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Answers "is transaction 0xabc... confirmed or did it fail", "what did this tx hash do", "what is the status of this transaction on Base". Takes a specific transaction reference and returns its details, status and effects: confirmed, reverted, pending or not_found, plus from, to, value_wei, value_eth, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status, and the decoded contract method where the calldata identifies one. Confidence scales with confirmation depth. Params: tx_hash (required, 0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth).

GAS_PRICE. Answers "what is gas right now on Ethereum", "how much does a transfer cost on Polygon", "are fees high on Base". Returns the current transaction fee level on a named chain in wei and gwei, plus the estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer. This is the fee to transact, not the price of the chain's token, which is CRYPTO_PRICE. Params: chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth).

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Answers "how much ETH does 0xabc... hold", "what is the USDC balance of this address on Arbitrum". Takes a specific blockchain address and returns its current native-coin or ERC-20 token balance on a named chain. Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth), token (optional, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, an ERC-20 contract address; when supplied, returns that token's balance instead of the chain's native coin).

TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT. Answers "how many wallets hold this token", "how many distinct addresses own 0xabc...". Takes a specific token contract address and returns the count of distinct holding addresses. This is a holder count, not price, supply or market data. Params: token (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).

TVL_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the TVL of Aave", "how much value is locked in Uniswap", "what is total value locked on Ethereum". Takes a named DeFi protocol, pool or chain and returns the total value locked in it in USD. This is value locked, not market capitalisation. When both a protocol and a chain are supplied it returns that protocol's TVL on that chain alongside its total across all chains. Params: exactly one of protocol (a DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap") or tvl_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum", covering DefiLlama's ~460 chains rather than only the five EVM chains above, which is why the param name differs from `chain`).

CRYPTO_PRICE. Answers "what is Bitcoin worth", "price of ETH in USD", "how much is the token at 0xabc... trading for". Names a cryptocurrency asset and returns its current USD price, with 24-hour change and market cap where the feed supplies them, cross-checked across independent sources and reported with a source count. For the cost of transacting on a chain use GAS_PRICE instead. Params: either coin_id alone (a CoinGecko id, e.g. "bitcoin"), or price_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "ethereum") together with token (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, the token's contract address). Exactly one of those two modes.

STOCK_PRICE. Answers "what is Apple trading at", "current share price of TSLA", "how much is NVDA stock". Names a listed equity or ticker and returns its current USD share price. Params: ticker (required, a stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL").

SSL_VERIFICATION. Answers "is the SSL certificate for example.com valid", "when does this domain's TLS certificate expire", "who issued the certificate for this host". Takes a hostname and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now, from a real live TLS handshake performed at request time rather than a cached or certificate-transparency lookup, which disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. Reports a named verdict (valid, expired, self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted), issuer, validity window, days to expiry, how many certificates the server presented and whether the chain reaches a trusted root, which name on the certificate the request matched, and the TLS version and cipher actually negotiated, flagging deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 that will fail for modern clients whatever the certificate says. Params: domain (required, a bare hostname such as "example.com", a full URL, a host:port pair, or a question naming the domain).

WEATHER_FORECAST. Answers "what's the weather in Tokyo the next three days", "will it rain in London tomorrow", "how windy will it be in Cape Town on Friday", "will it snow in Oslo next week", and coordinate forms such as "what is the forecast at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?". Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and answers the specific thing asked: the day or window named (right now, today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday, this weekend, this week, in N hours, the next N days or hours) and the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature), leading with a direct yes or no on that aspect the way a person would answer, then giving the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, precipitation total and chance of precipitation, snowfall, and peak wind speed with gusts and direction. Read live from the forecast service at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), days (optional, 1-16), when (optional, overrides the window parsed from the question), focus (optional, one of rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature).

STORM_ALERT. Reports storm risk at a location over a stated window, answering questions of the form "what is the storm risk at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?" and "what is the storm risk at latitude -5.1486, longitude 119.4319 right now?", as well as "is there a storm risk in Miami this weekend". Reports exactly what such a question asks for: wind speed, gusts, precipitation, and an overall risk between 0 and 1. Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and reads the window from it ("right now", "in N hours", "over the next 48 hours", "this weekend"). Alongside the 0-1 risk score a contract can threshold on, it returns a disruption grade (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE) from peak wind gust and its Beaufort force named in plain words, sustained wind speed and direction, total precipitation, forecast thunderstorm and hail hours, and the operational response that grade calls for. The window runs from the current hour forward, not from midnight, so the peak gust reported is always still ahead. Read live at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), hours (optional, default 48, also read from the question).

IP_GEOLOCATION. Answers "where is 8.8.8.8 located", "what country is this IP address from", "is this IP a VPN or a datacenter". Takes an IPv4 or IPv6 address and reports its country, region, city, postal code, coordinates, timezone, and network owner with ASN, plus privacy and risk flags saying whether the address is a known proxy or VPN exit, a hosting or datacenter network, or a mobile carrier network, which is what fraud, bot-screening and geo-gating callers actually need. Read live at request time. Confidence is reported as 0.95 rather than 1.0 because IP geolocation is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city. Params: ip (required, a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address such as "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888", or a whole question naming one).

ACADEMIC_SEARCH. Answers "find papers on federated learning", "peer-reviewed research on fraud detection since 2020". Takes a topic, or the whole question, and lists peer-reviewed journal articles on it in relevance order, with preprints, theses and datasets excluded, naming every paper found in the answer itself with its title, authors, publishing journal, year, citation count and DOI, plus a real excerpt from the leading paper's abstract and a note on which of the results is the most cited. A date range stated in the question ("since 2020", "between 2010 and 2020") is applied. Read live from OpenAlex, with Crossref as a fallback, at request time. Params: topic (required), limit (optional, 1-25, default 5), from_year (optional), to_year (optional).

WEB_SEARCH. Answers an open question of any kind from a live web search performed at request time, for questions that have no single authoritative feed behind them: "what happened at the summit this week", "how does a heat pump work", "will El Nino disrupt shipping this season", "what did the company announce". Takes the whole question as the caller wrote it and returns a direct written answer followed by the sources it drew on, naming the most relevant three with their URLs. Questions about current events are searched against a news index and questions about markets and company results against a finance index, chosen from the wording of the question itself. Confidence is reported as 0.9 rather than 1.0 because a synthesized web answer is only as reliable as the pages behind it, unlike a chain read or a live TLS handshake. For a peer-reviewed literature search use ACADEMIC_SEARCH instead, and for a live number such as a price, gas fee, balance or forecast use the specific intent for it, which reads the value from its own provider rather than from the open web. Params: query (required, the whole question), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 5), topic_mode (optional, one of general, news, finance, overriding what the question implies).

FRAUD_DETECTION. Answers "was BitConnect a scam", "is this scheme fraudulent", "what happened in the FTX fraud". Assesses how likely a named entity, scheme or action is to be fraudulent, answering from source-backed fraud knowledge rather than speculation, and returning INCONCLUSIVE rather than guessing when the record does not support a verdict. JSON body: { "query": "..." } (8 to 1000 characters).

FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address. Answers "is 0xabc... a scam wallet", "how risky is this address", "is it safe to receive funds from this wallet". Returns a 0-1 risk score with named contributing signals, checked against a built-in registry of over 2,600 known entities (OFAC-sanctioned addresses, reported scam addresses, exchange and bridge wallets, mixers and burn addresses) so that known-legitimate infrastructure is not flagged as fraud. Risk and confidence are reported separately: a low-risk verdict from bounded scanning is returned as low risk with low confidence rather than overstated. Params: wallet (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address, identical to the GET form above and accepting the address in a JSON body instead of the query string. JSON body: { "wallet": "0x..." }.

answer.description: The graded answer: one self-contained sentence stating the result and the facts behind it, on every endpoint. This is the field named by semantics.signal_mapping.label_field. It repeats `summary` unless a route supplies its own fuller wording (the fraud routes do).

as_of.description: ISO timestamp of the source reading on gas, balance, holders, TVL, crypto and stock routes. On /stock-price this is the provider's quote observation time and is null when the provider did not supply one; it is never replaced by the response retrieval time.

asn.description: /ip-geolocate only. Autonomous system number and name.

authorization_error.description: /ssl-check only. Reason authorized is false, e.g. a self-signed or expired certificate.

authorized.description: /ssl-check only. Whether Node's default trust store accepts the certificate chain.

balance_native.description: /wallet-balance only. Human-normalized amount. Always present for native balance; null for an ERC-20 balance if Blockscout didn't recognize the token (decimals unknown, balance_wei still valid).

balance_wei.description: /wallet-balance only. Raw integer amount, native wei or the ERC-20's smallest unit depending on whether token was supplied.

beaufort_description.description: /storm-alert only. That Beaufort force in plain words, e.g. "gale".

beaufort_force.description: /storm-alert only. Beaufort force of the peak gust.

block_hash.description: /check-tx only. Null while pending / no receipt yet.

block_number.description: Null while pending / no receipt yet, or if the block-number read failed best-effort.

canonical.description: Compact deterministic one-line verdict summary, shape varies per endpoint (documented in each route's description).

chain_complete.description: /ssl-check only. Null when the host is unreachable and the chain cannot be inspected.

chain_length.description: /ssl-check only. How many certificates the server itself presented. Excludes the trust anchor the local store supplies, which the server did not send.

chain_tvl_usd.description: /tvl only. Protocol TVL on the requested chain when both protocol and tvl_chain are supplied.

change_24h_pct.description: /crypto-price only. CoinPaprika 24-hour USD price change percentage when available.

checked_at.description: ISO timestamp of the live read, on /ssl-check, /weather-forecast, /storm-alert, /ip-geolocate and /academic-search.

company_name.description: /stock-price only. Provider-supplied company name, or null when the provider omitted it.

condition.description: /weather-forecast only. Expected condition in plain words, from the WMO weather code.

covers_hostnames.description: /ssl-check only. Every DNS name and IP the certificate covers.

currency.description: /stock-price only. Exact provider denomination, including case when it distinguishes units such as GBp (pence) from GBP (pounds).

days.description: /weather-forecast only. Day-by-day breakdown of every field above.

exchange.description: /stock-price only. The exchange the ticker trades on.

fee_usd.description: /gas-price only. Estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer at the current gas price. Null if the native token's USD price could not be looked up — gas_price_wei/gwei are still valid in that case.

fingerprint_sha256.description: /ssl-check only. SHA-256 fingerprint of the leaf certificate.

focus.description: /weather-forecast only. The aspect the answer leads with, as understood from the request.

from_year.description: /academic-search only. Earliest publication year applied, whether passed or read from the question.

holders_count.description: /token-holders only. Null when status is not_found.

hostname_valid.description: /ssl-check only. Null when the host is unreachable and hostname validation cannot run.

hours_assessed.description: /storm-alert only. Length of the assessed window in hours.

is_hosting.description: /ip-geolocate only. Address belongs to a hosting or datacenter network rather than a residential connection.

is_mobile.description: /ip-geolocate only. Address belongs to a mobile carrier network.

is_proxy_or_vpn.description: /ip-geolocate only. Address is a known proxy or VPN exit.

issuer.description: /ssl-check only. Certificate authority organization or common name.

key_bits.description: /ssl-check only. Certificate public key size in bits.

label.description: Sentinel fraud verdict, also returned as status for TxLens compatibility.

location.description: /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. The resolved place, as name, region, country.

market_cap_usd.description: /crypto-price only. Current CoinPaprika market capitalization when available.

matched_hostname.description: /ssl-check only. Which name on the certificate the requested host matched, wildcards included. Null on a hostname mismatch.

max_wind_speed_kmh.description: /storm-alert only. Strongest sustained wind in the window.

method.description: /check-tx only. Decoded contract method name when available.

method_selector.description: /check-tx only. First four calldata bytes for contract calls.

method_signature.description: /check-tx only. Decoded contract method signature when available.

most_cited.description: /academic-search only. Whichever returned paper carries the most citations. Reported alongside the results, not used to order them.

native_price_usd.description: /gas-price only. USD price of the chain's native gas token used to compute fee_usd. Null under the same condition as fee_usd.

org.description: /ip-geolocate only. Registrant organization, when it differs from the operator.

papers.description: /academic-search only. Each entry carries title, year, citation_count, authors, venue, doi and abstract_snippet. Listed in relevance order.

peak_gust_kmh.description: /storm-alert and /weather-forecast. Strongest wind gust in the window.

peak_gust_time.description: /storm-alert only. Local time of the strongest gust. Always inside the future window.

peak_wind_kmh.description: /weather-forecast only. Highest sustained wind across the window.

precipitation_probability_max_pct.description: /weather-forecast only. Peak chance of precipitation across the window.

precipitation_total_mm.description: /weather-forecast only. Total precipitation across the window.

price.description: /stock-price only. The listing price in the units named by currency.

price_source.description: /crypto-price and /stock-price. Which upstream actually supplied the selected price.

price_usd.description: /crypto-price and /stock-price. On /stock-price this is populated only when the provider quote is denominated in USD; it is null for non-USD listings and when status is not_found.

protocol.description: /ssl-check only. TLS version actually negotiated, e.g. TLSv1.3.

protocol_deprecated.description: /ssl-check only. True for TLS 1.0/1.1, which most modern clients refuse regardless of certificate validity.

protocol_total_tvl_usd.description: /tvl only. Total protocol TVL across all chains when both protocol and tvl_chain are supplied.

provider.description: /web-search only. Which search service supplied the answer.

query.description: Echoes the main lookup value on routes that return it, including TVL, crypto, stock, weather and academic search.

query_type.description: /tvl and /crypto-price only. Which query mode the request used (protocol/chain for /tvl, coin_id/chain_token for /crypto-price).

reason.description: Complete fraud answer or wallet-risk explanation.

receipt_status.description: /check-tx only. Explicit receipt outcome, independent of `status`. Null while pending / not found (no receipt exists yet).

recommended_action.description: /storm-alert only. The operational response the risk grade calls for.

result_count.description: /web-search only. How many web sources the answer drew on.

retrieved_at.description: /stock-price only. ISO timestamp when TxLens retrieved the quote, distinct from provider observation time in as_of.

risk_level.description: Named risk grade. LOW/ELEVATED/HIGH/NOT_APPLICABLE on /assess-wallet; LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE on /storm-alert.

search_query.description: /web-search only. The text actually sent to the search index, after an instruction aimed at the miner ("search the web for ...") has been removed from the front of the question.

severe_hail_hours.description: /storm-alert only. Forecast hours with a hail-bearing thunderstorm.

snowfall_total_cm.description: /weather-forecast only. Total snowfall across the window.

source_count.description: /crypto-price only. Number of independent price feeds that answered.

status.description: confirmed/reverted/pending/not_found/error on /check-tx; ok/error on /gas-price and /wallet-balance (live reads have no confirmation states); ok/not_found/error on /token-holders (not_found means the address isn't a known ERC-20 token on that chain, not a failure). Fraud routes may use Sentinel's named verdict. A Sentinel outage is inconclusive rather than a failed HTTP request. invalid_input can be returned by any endpoint and is an answer, not a failure: it means the parameters supplied could not identify anything to look up, and summary explains in plain language what the endpoint needs instead. It is returned with HTTP 200 and no error field, because the input was unusable rather than TxLens being unable to serve.

tvl_usd.description: /tvl only. Null when status is not_found.

Assesses an Ethereum address for fraud risk using registries, funding relationships, contract controls, and bounded on-chain evidence. JSON body: { "wallet": "0x..." } (required).

name: Elcaro IPI Detector
description: Detects indirect prompt injection in content an AI agent has retrieved but not yet acted on — emails, search results, web pages, documents, code. Returns a calibrated 0-1 risk score, a risk band, and the specific injection techniques found with evidence for each, across a six-class taxonomy: authority framing, delimiter confusion, task reframing, obfuscation, placement salience, and conditional triggers. Rule-based rather than LLM-based, so verdicts are deterministic and land in single-digit milliseconds instead of adding another model call to the agent's hot path.

endpoints.description: Scan untrusted retrieved text for indirect prompt injection. Required body field is `content` (the email, search snippet, page, document, or code). Optional `content_type` weights risk by provenance. Returns risk_score (0-1), risk_level (safe/low/suspicious/dangerous), flagged_techniques, and a one-sentence summary.

content_type.description: Provenance of the content, which sets contextual weighting. Fully untrusted sources (email, search_result, webpage) weight highest; chat_message is the user's own input and weights lowest.

context.description: Optional detail about the consuming agent or task. Accepts an object or a string; informational only and does not affect the verdict.

deep_analysis.description: Run a semantic second pass on gray-zone results. Rule-based only unless the operator has configured a classifier; otherwise ignored.

content_type.description: The content type the verdict applies to.

deep_analysis_used.description: Whether the semantic second pass actually ran.

indicators.description: One threat card per finding: technique, severity, confidence, the matched text with surrounding context, an explanation, remediation advice, and MITRE ATLAS / Elcaro TTP references.

risk_level.description: Banded verdict. safe <0.2, low <0.5, suspicious <0.7, dangerous >=0.7. Treat suspicious and dangerous as "do not act on this content".

risk_score.description: Injection risk. 0 is clean, 1 is a certain injection attempt.

summary.description: One-sentence human-readable verdict.

limitations.message: Scans a single payload per request. Chunk very large documents client-side; detection operates only on the text supplied in one call.
Detects indirect prompt injection techniques only. Not a malware scanner, PII detector, or general toxicity classifier.
Patterns are tuned for English content. Non-English injections may score below their true risk.

name: Legwork Job Hunter
description:
Live job search and job-application writing, answered from real job boards on every single call — never from a cached index, a stale scrape, or a language model's memory of what was hiring last year.

WHAT IT DOES — TWO CAPABILITIES.

(1) JOB SEARCH. Send the user's request exactly as they wrote it — "senior backend engineer, TypeScript, remote, $150k+", "who is hiring registered nurses in Austin", "what does a data analyst earn in New York", "entry level government jobs" — and get back a ranked shortlist of roles that are open right now, queried live at request time from three independent boards — Adzuna (commercial listings worldwide), USAJOBS (the official US federal board) and Remotive (remote-first roles) — so a search is not hostage to any single board's coverage or uptime. Every match returns the job title, the hiring company, the location, whether it is remote, the real posted salary range, a direct link to the live posting, the board it came from, and an explained 0-100 match score. The score is a published rubric rather than a black-box percentage: skills 40 points, pay 20, location 15, seniority 15, and the caller's own stated priorities 10. Each axis returns its own number AND a one-line reason, so a caller can see exactly why the first result outranked the second, and can defend that ranking to the person who asked.

PAY QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED WITH A NUMBER. Ask "what does a data analyst earn in New York" or "how much do registered nurses make in Austin" and the reply is the actual figure — median, typical range and full observed range — computed from the live postings that publish a salary, with the sample size stated and postings without a published salary excluded rather than guessed at. These are advertised salaries from openings that are live right now, not survey data.

(2) APPLICATION WRITING. Send any job-search writing task — "write a cover letter for this role", "tailor my resume to this posting", "draft a follow-up email after my interview", "write a LinkedIn summary", "write a cold outreach note to this recruiter" — optionally together with the candidate's real resume and the target job posting. It returns a finished, ready-to-send document: a tailored resume, a cover letter, an email subject line and an email body, addressed to the named role and company. Documents are written strictly from the facts the caller actually supplied — no employer, job title, date, degree or metric is ever invented, and any genuinely missing personal detail is left as one clearly marked [placeholder] rather than fabricated.

ROUTE ANY OF THESE HERE: open jobs, job openings, who is hiring, job hunting, job boards, career moves, what a role pays, salary ranges by job title or by city, compensation benchmarks, remote work listings, federal and government jobs, hiring in a named city or country, plus resumes, CVs, cover letters, application emails, recruiter outreach, interview follow-ups, thank-you notes and LinkedIn profile summaries.

DO NOT ROUTE HERE FOR: general web search, current news, academic or scientific research, company financials or stock data, or open-ended conversation unrelated to work and hiring.

RELIABILITY CONTRACT. This miner always answers with HTTP 2xx and a complete, scoreable signal — label, confidence and reason are present on every response without exception, including for malformed or empty input. Confidence is honest and self-assessed rather than a flattering constant: it is high when the live boards answered and produced real matches, and it degrades openly when a source fails or the market genuinely returns nothing, so a caller is never handed a thin answer dressed up as a strong one.

endpoints.description: Search live job boards (Adzuna, USAJOBS, Remotive) and return either a ranked, scored shortlist of open roles, or — when the request asks what something PAYS — a computed salary answer (median, quartile range and sample size) synthesised from the live postings. Requests naming no occupation or skill are declined rather than answered with unrelated listings. Only postings genuinely about the requested occupation are returned — an unrelated listing is dropped rather than ranked, so an empty shortlist means the market is empty, not that the filter was loose. Send the user's complete job-search request verbatim as query — it is parsed into structured criteria (roles, seniority, locations, salary floor, skills). Structured fields may be sent alongside to pin the criteria exactly. Every match returns title, company, location, salary range, posting URL, source board and an explained 0-100 rubric score (skills 40 / pay 20 / location 15 / seniority 15 / extra factors 10). Use for any question about open postings, hiring, or what a role pays.

Write job-application documents: a tailored resume, a cover letter, an application email, recruiter outreach, an interview follow-up or a LinkedIn summary. Scoped to job-application writing — a general writing task (a poem, an essay, code) is declined rather than answered with a cover letter. Send the writing task verbatim as prompt — "write a cover letter for the Senior Engineer role at Acme" — and optionally the structured objects candidate (name, resumeText, skills, email) and posting (title, company, description) for a fully tailored draft drawn strictly from the candidate's real experience; nothing is ever invented. With structured input the response carries resume, coverLetter, emailSubject and emailBody; with a prompt alone it carries the best draft possible from stated facts plus generatedText. Use for any writing task about resumes, cover letters, applications, outreach or job-search materials.

name: Truvian Exact On-Chain Truth Engine
description: Deterministic, exactly-verifiable on-chain answers for Base and Ethereum, read live from JSON-RPC at request time. ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP returns the full canonical facts of a transaction — status, block, addresses, value, gas, and the true total fee including the OP-stack L1 data fee that naive implementations drop — decoded ERC-20 transfers included. GAS_PRICE returns a block-anchored fee snapshot with EIP-1559 percentiles and L1 base fee. Every response leads with a number-first plain-language answer followed by the complete structured payload, and every figure is independently reproducible from public RPC.

endpoints.description: Look up a transaction by hash (ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP). Params: hash (or tx_hash/txHash, or a query containing one), chain (default base). Returns status, block, from/to, value, gas used, effective gas price, exact total fee in wei including L1 data fee, and decoded ERC-20 transfers.

Current gas prices for a chain (GAS_PRICE). Params: chain (default base) or a natural-language query. Returns eth_gasPrice, base fee, priority fee, 5-block EIP-1559 percentiles, and L1 base fee, all anchored to an explicit block number.
